@bananamanzero @iidx_gone @flow_mein *A little long talk about my thoughts*

I did a chiptune live in Japan for a short period of time. Among them, "GAMEBOY performer" felt DJ style performance is more powerful than live style.

928468026516635648.t:
@bananamanzero @iidx_gone @flow_mein Because they are good at attracting spectators as they see the audience's reactions and select tracks and connect them in real time.

but, since I wanted to play GAMEBOY as a musical instrument rather than as a record, I was seeking a way to not become a DJ.

928468289088495616.t: @bananamanzero @iidx_gone @flow_mein So until I appeared in SST2017 I repeated trial and error on how I can establish a live style with only GAMEBOY (I stuffed dozens of tracks in one lsdsng, changed the parameters of the tone in real time, pulled out the cartridge during playing the song and freeze the playback🤔)

928468467421814784.t: @bananamanzero @iidx_gone @flow_mein What I noticed by trial and error is that these technical performances may be exciting for the performers, but to the audience it was only possible to tell like Secret ingredient.

928468643209342976.t: @bananamanzero @iidx_gone @flow_mein So I used these techniques in SST2017 and tried to behave like punk musician. I made about 20 songs I wanted to listen with live, (I only made songs that I wanted to listen to at home…) and played about 20 songs like a medley.

928468827809050624.t: @bananamanzero @iidx_gone @flow_mein After the live show, I think the "live style" felt that the movement of the performer, the groove, and the corresponding resonance of the speaker were most reflected in the excitement of the audience.
